fields.description:
Stop `rebar init` from silently creating an empty divergent store when it cannot obtain the configured tickets branch. This fixes P1 `01e8-302b`.

## Current mechanism

`_mount_or_create_branch` currently checks only local refs and the local remote-tracking ref. If both are absent, it immediately creates an orphan branch. A failed or timed-out fetch can therefore make an existing remote branch look like a genuine first init. `pending_init_attaches_to_existing` repeats the same ref-only predicate, and `src/rebar/_cli/_init.py` calls that predicate from both best-effort mount and strict auto-init, so all of those callers must share the same result and distinguish unreachable from genuinely absent.

The current code already bounds the cold materializing fetch with `_git_fetch` and `_FETCH_TIMEOUT = 300`. Preserve that behavior. Add a shorter bounded remote-advertisement probe through a shared network runner rather than duplicating the timeout wrapper. Use `git ls-remote --exit-code <remote> refs/heads/<branch>` so its three outcomes are explicit: return code 0 means advertised, 2 means reachable but absent, and timeout/other failures mean unreachable.

## Implementation plan

- Generalize the existing bounded Git-network seam so `_git_fetch` retains its 300-second cold-fetch contract and a new advertisement probe uses a short named timeout. Both convert `TimeoutExpired` to a descriptive `CompletedProcess(124)`.
- Add one shared tri-state remote-branch probe consumed by `_mount_or_create_branch`, `pending_init_attaches_to_existing`, and the auto-init decisions in `src/rebar/_cli/_init.py` whenever neither a local branch nor a local remote-tracking ref exists.
- Cache only the tri-state probe result for a short named TTL, keyed by resolved repo/remote/branch. The first best-effort-mount probe and the immediately following strict auto-init reuse one result, so an unreachable remote costs at most one probe timeout per CLI invocation. A test advances the clock past the TTL and proves later calls re-probe, avoiding stale long-lived-library state.
- Update `_create_tracker` in `src/rebar/_cli/_init.py` to distinguish reachable-absent from unreachable. Unreachable fails closed with the remote diagnostic and never falls through to the interactive consent gate. Best-effort mount remains non-raising, while the following strict gate reuses the cached result and emits the actionable failure.
- If the remote advertises the branch, attempt the existing bounded fetch. Mount only after the branch materializes; if fetch fails, return nonzero with an error naming the configured remote/branch and the fetch-and-retry remediation. Never create an orphan in this state.
- If the remote is reachable and does not advertise the branch, preserve legitimate first-init orphan bootstrap.
- If the probe cannot reach the remote or times out, fail closed with a distinct error naming the remote, branch, timeout, retry remediation, and the explicit deliberate-bootstrap override. Never create an orphan unless the override was supplied.
- Add `--force-new-store` to the explicit CLI, thread `force_new_store=False` through `init_core`, and expose the equivalent keyword on `rebar.init_repo`. Auto-init intentionally never supplies the override: only an operator's explicit CLI flag or library keyword can authorize bootstrap while reachability is unknown.
- The override applies only to the unreachable outcome. When the remote is reachable, emit a warning that `--force-new-store` has no effect and continue the normal path: reachable-absent bootstraps normally; advertised fetches/mounts or fails nonzero without orphaning.
- Update init help and generated CLI reference for the new flag.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With a reachable remote advertising the configured tickets branch but no local remote-tracking ref, a simulated bounded fetch failure returns nonzero and creates no orphan branch. Tier: CLI subprocess with real temporary repositories.
- [ ] With a reachable remote that does not advertise the configured branch, init still bootstraps successfully. Tier: CLI subprocess negative control.
- [ ] With an unreachable or timing-out remote, explicit init and strict auto-init return nonzero within one probe bound, create no orphan branch, and emit an error distinct from the advertised/fetch-failed case. Strict auto-init does not enter the consent prompt. Tier: CLI subprocess with deterministic fault injection at the Git network seam. Proving command: `pytest tests/integration/test_init_fail_closed.py -k unreachable -v`.
- [ ] `rebar init --force-new-store` and `rebar.init_repo(force_new_store=True)` permit deliberate bootstrap only when reachability cannot be established. Tier: CLI subprocess plus library interface test.
- [ ] With a reachable advertised branch, `--force-new-store` is ineffective: the command warns, attempts the normal bounded fetch, and returns nonzero without an orphan if that fetch fails. With reachable-absent, it warns and follows the normal successful bootstrap path. Tier: CLI subprocess negative controls.
- [ ] Failure messages name the configured remote, configured branch, timeout where applicable, and concrete fetch/retry or force-new-store remediation. Tier: unit assertions on stderr.
- [ ] An existing healthy store remains idempotent, does not invoke the advertisement probe, and is unaffected by the override default. Tier: CLI subprocess. Proving command: `pytest tests/integration/test_init_fail_closed.py -k idempotent -v`.
- [ ] `pending_init_attaches_to_existing` returns true when the remote advertises the branch even though the local remote-tracking ref is absent, and false for reachable-absent and unreachable outcomes. Tier: unit test with a real temporary remote. Proving command: `pytest tests/unit/test_init_attach_predicate.py -v`.
- [ ] Behavioral wiring tests monkeypatch the one shared probe and prove `_mount_or_create_branch`, `pending_init_attaches_to_existing`, and both `_cli/_init.py` mount paths consume it; a second independent remote-existence predicate would fail the tests.
- [ ] One CLI invocation performs at most one underlying advertisement probe on the unreachable path; advancing the injected monotonic clock past the short TTL causes a fresh probe. Tier: unit orchestration test.
- [ ] Existing timeout tests continue proving the cold fetch retains its 300-second bound, while new tests prove the advertisement probe has its own positive short bound and folds timeout to return code 124.

## Files

`src/rebar/_commands/init.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/_init.py`, `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/help/init.txt`, generated `docs/cli-reference.md`, and tests.

Scope: S-M. No dependencies.
